VICTORYHEALTH ANALYTICS | SYNTHETIC PORTFOLIO STUDY

MedSafe-R: reliability and safety

Corrected v1.3 data. Snapshot 31 July 2026. All data and labels are synthetic; no clinical or deployment claims.

01 overdue pm02 downtime recurrence03 maintenance comparisons04 safety associations05 failure models05b safety models

Main findings

  • Overdue PM: 253 devices (21.1%); log-only evidence gives 491 overdue among 1161 devices with a recorded PM, with 39 unknown.
  • Corrective repairs account for 76.3% of recorded maintenance downtime. 130 devices have at least 3 recorded repairs.
  • Failure in the next 30 days: logistic AUC 0.608; random forest 0.679; heuristic 0.703.
  • Safety event in the next 90 days: logistic AUC 0.557; random forest 0.582; heuristic 0.619.

Methods and limitations

  1. All records, manufacturers, regulatory signals and outcomes are synthetic. Results show analytical methods, not validated device risk or patient-safety benefits.
  2. Snapshot: 31 July 2026. Historical event windows are exactly 90 days (3 May-31 July 2026) and 365 days (1 August 2025-31 July 2026), inclusive. July telemetry is a calendar month; utilisation is the May-July mean.
  3. Overdue PM uses the later of inventory and valid logged PM. Source coverage: 550 log-supported, 639 inventory-only, 11 commissioning placeholders. The latter do not prove PM occurred. Sensitivity counts use a different evidence denominator.
  4. Nine monthly records fail hours plausibility checks. They are excluded from hours/utilisation analysis; none is in May-July. Reported downtime uses maintenance logs, not monthly operations; missing commissioning-month exposure remains an assumption.
  5. Corrective repairs are not guaranteed independent failures. Repeat jobs within 90 days may be unrelated categories. Mean repair intervals are calendar gaps, not operating-hour MTBF; legacy 999 values are excluded from modelling.
  6. Safety affected-device counts use distinct device IDs. Historical associations use binary presence of an event in the same 365-day period and do not establish event ordering or causality. Wilson intervals are descriptive only.
  7. Learning pipelines fit preprocessing only on training folds. Models have fixed settings, no hyperparameter search. No legacy MTBF, ID, priority score/band, synthetic quality score or target enters the trained predictors. Missing repair intervals are imputed within folds with indicators.
  8. Cross-validation assesses synthetic-label discrimination among held-out devices in the same dataset. It is not prospective, temporal or external validation. Some predictors and labels may share generator logic, and labels have not been checked against future event records.
  9. Conditional bootstrap AUC intervals quantify resampling uncertainty for fixed OOF scores. They do not capture model refitting, correlated site effects or uncertainty in the data generator. Comparisons are descriptive, not significance tests.
  10. Class weighting and resampling are not used; rare-event performance is reported with average precision, Brier score (trained probability models only), and positives found in a fixed top-120 review budget. No deployment threshold is validated. Calibration requires further study.
  11. CSV tables, fold assignments/predictions, exact environment versions and source hash are included. Run python analysis.py after installing requirements.txt. Each HTML chart has a corresponding table view; chart images themselves are static.
